1.title: 8강 1번 (50P)
1.q1: 어법상 옳지 않은 선지와, 그 이유는?
1.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
1.passage: Triangle enthusiast Pythagoras thought a lot about music. He studied the lyre, a stringed instrument that was kind of a handheld harp, and developed the mathematics around ① how tone changes with string length. Strike a lyre string and you contribute energy to it, making the string vibrate at a particular frequency that’s a function of its length; your ears experience ② that vibrating energy as a specific tone, like B-flat. Pythagoras believed that everything in the natural world ③ was similarly ruled by math. When he looked up at the night sky, he didn’t just see stars and planets — he saw an elegant equation at work. He believed that each planet emitted a different sound as it rotated and revolved, like the strings of a lyre, each ④ contributes a unique celestial tone to a beautiful cosmic symphony. This concept became ⑤ known as “the music of the spheres.”
1.key_points: 답은 4번이야. 분사구문 contributing을 써야 하는 자리야.

2.title: 8강 2번 (51P)
2.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
2.passage:
The growing divergence of American communities is important not just in itself but because of what it means for American society. ① While the divide is first and foremost economic, it is now beginning to affect cultural identity, health, family stability, and even politics. ② The sorting of highly educated Americans into some communities and less educated Americans into others tends to
magnify and intensify all other socioeconomic differences. ③ For example, there are vast differences in life expectancy among inhabitants of American cities, and these differences have been expanding for the past three decades. ④ Rather than isolating differences, successful societies create space for them to coexist and enrich the broader community. ⑤ The divorce rates, crime rates, and political clout of different communities have also been diverging. These trends are reshaping the very fabric of our society.
2.key_points: 4번이 정답이야. 본문에서 전개하는 '미국 사회의 분열이 초래하는 문제점에 대한 객관적 기술'이 아닌, 이상적 사회에 대한 제언의 개념이므로 서술이 틀려.

3.title: 8강 3번 (52P)
3.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
3.passage:
A few bird species, such as the Woodpecker Finch of the Galápagos Islands, use tools to extract
food. Seventeen species of birds have been shown either in the field or in laboratory
studies to craft tools, usually but not always for use in foraging.

(A) Knowing the overall details of nest construction is mostly innate, but assembling nests also
requires thought and skill. Birds must find and collect material, which in itself requires some
measure of searching and remembering, a form of cognitive behavior.

(B) This, of course, is but a small percentage of the total number of bird species, which is
approximately 10,000 worldwide. Tool use remains uncommon in birds.

(C) But consider bird nests. The pioneer American ornithologist Alexander Wilson described in detail
how a female Orchard Oriole intricately weaves grasses to form the hanging nest. Constructing
an oriole nest would be challenging for any human.
3.key_points: 올바른 순서는 B C A 야.

4.title: 8강 4번 (53P)
4.q3: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 요약하면?
4.passage:
Children come by their excitement naturally. Until it gets crushed out of them in school, kids
innately know how to have fun and love what they do.

(A) But as Csikszentmihalyi noted, “Most enjoyable activities are not natural; they demand an effort
that initially one is reluctant to make.” Some activities will only engross us if we take the
trouble to pay close attention to them.

(B) Simply put, flow is when your concentration is such that you lose all sense of time and place.
The experience is its own reward; its end goal or outcome is just the icing on the cake. The
satisfactions that go with creating an inspired work of art or flawlessly executing an athletic feat
are easy enough to imagine.

(C) Give them a wooden stick and watch as they begin to play with it. Wait a while and ask them
what it is. You will get answers like “It’s a car!” or “It’s a rocket!” Kids have an
unlimited capacity not just for fantasy and imagination but for engrossment, much as artists or
athletes do when they are experiencing the mental state that my mentor Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi
famously described as “flow.”
